# E0508: function parameter that escapes

A function parameter passes its effects through to the caller, so it is only called during the call. Mark it `escaping` to keep it, and its row is then exactly the one written.

- Rule: [`effects.no-escape`](../../reference/12-effects.md#effects.no-escape)
- Reported at: the first use that keeps the parameter: the parameter's name, or the closure literal that names it.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `analyses` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0508:3
type Button = { label: str, on_click: fn() / io }

fn button(label: str, on_click: fn() / io) -> Button { Button { label, on_click } }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
type Button = { label: str, on_click: fn() / io }

fn button(label: str, escaping on_click: fn() / io) -> Button { Button { label, on_click } }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0508_function_parameter_that_escapes.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0508_function_parameter_that_escapes.lt):

```text
── FUNCTION PARAMETER THAT ESCAPES ── E0508_function_parameter_that_escapes.lt:3:72  [E0508]

`on_click` is kept, but its effects pass through to the caller:

  3 │ fn button(label: str, on_click: fn() / io) -> Button { Button { label, on_click } }
    │                       ──────── its effects pass through
    │                                                                        ^^^^^^^^ stored in a `Button` here

A function parameter passes its effects through to the caller, so it is only
called during the call. Mark it `escaping` to keep it, and its row is then
exactly the one written.

To fix it, mark `on_click` `escaping`, so its row is exactly the one written:

  3 │ fn button(label: str, escaping on_click: fn() / io) -> Button { Button { label, on_click } }
    │                       +++++++++
```
